_about: Hand-written key points for pyt-community-medicine.html (27 Nov 2026, lead). Samples: FMGE recalls, no images.
subject: Community Medicine (PSM)
intro: PSM is one of FMGE's highest-scoring subjects: formulas, schedules, programmes and cut-offs that are asked almost word for word every year. These are the topics that keep coming back, most-asked first, with the one thing to remember about each.

psm.epi.design.note: Case-control: start from disease, look back at exposure; gives the odds ratio; good for rare diseases. Cohort: start from exposure, follow forward; gives incidence and relative risk. RCT: the best evidence; randomisation removes confounding, blinding removes observer bias. Hawthorne effect: people behave differently when watched.
psm.epi.design.why: Changing behaviour because one knows one is being observed is the Hawthorne effect.

psm.epi.meas.note: Incidence = new cases in a period; prevalence = all existing cases (prevalence = incidence × duration). Crude death rate uses the mid-year population (1 July). IMR per 1,000 live births; MMR per 100,000 live births. Case fatality rate shows how deadly a disease is.
psm.epi.meas.why: Rates use the mid-year population, counted on 1 July.

psm.epi.risk.note: Relative risk = incidence in exposed ÷ incidence in unexposed (cohort). Odds ratio = ad/bc (case-control). Attributable risk = incidence in exposed − incidence in unexposed; as a percentage of the exposed incidence it shows how much could be prevented. NNT = 1 ÷ absolute risk reduction.

psm.epi.screen.note: Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN), true positive rate, good for ruling out. Specificity = TN/(TN+FP), good for ruling in. PPV = TP/(TP+FP), rises with prevalence; NPV falls as prevalence rises. Sensitivity and specificity do not change with prevalence.
psm.epi.screen.why: Of 10,000 people, 100 are sick: 80 true positives; 9,900 well: 990 false positives. PPV = 80 ÷ 1,070 ≈ 7.5%.

psm.epi.trans.note: Secondary attack rate = new cases among susceptible contacts ÷ total susceptible contacts (the first case excluded), within one incubation period. Herd immunity protects the unvaccinated when enough are immune. Chronic carriers shed the organism for a long time (typhoid: gallbladder).
psm.epi.trans.why: Chronic carriers keep shedding the organism for a long time, like typhoid carriers.

psm.epi.nat.note: Levels of prevention: primordial (stop risk factors from arising, e.g. healthy habits in children), primary (before disease: vaccines, hand washing), secondary (early diagnosis and treatment: screening), tertiary (limit disability and rehabilitate).
psm.epi.nat.why: Screening finds disease early, before symptoms: that is secondary prevention.

psm.bio.central.note: Mean is pulled by outliers; median is best for skewed data; mode is the most frequent value. Measures of spread: range, standard deviation, variance, coefficient of variation (SD/mean × 100). Standard error measures how precise a sample estimate is, not spread.

psm.bio.normal.note: A bell-shaped curve: mean = median = mode. About 68% of values lie within 1 SD, 95% within 2 SD (1.96 exactly), 99.7% within 3 SD. Skewed right: mean > median > mode.
psm.bio.normal.why: About 68% of values fall within one standard deviation of the mean.

psm.bio.hyp.note: p under 0.05 is called significant. Type I error (α): saying there is a difference when there is none; type II (β): missing a real difference; power = 1 − β. Tests: paired t-test (same group before and after), unpaired t-test (two groups), ANOVA (3+ groups), chi-square (proportions).
psm.bio.hyp.why: The same patients measured before and after the drug: a paired t-test.

psm.bio.samp.note: Simple random: every unit has an equal chance. Systematic: every kth unit. Stratified: random samples from each subgroup (good when groups differ). Cluster: whole groups such as villages (used in immunisation surveys, 30 × 7). Snowball: subjects refer others (hidden populations).
psm.bio.samp.why: Recruiting through referrals from earlier subjects is snowball sampling.

psm.vac.nis.note: Pregnancy: Td 2 doses 4 weeks apart, or one booster if fully vaccinated in the last 3 years. Children: BCG, OPV-0 and hepatitis B at birth; pentavalent, OPV and rotavirus at 6, 10, 14 weeks; MR at 9-12 and 16-24 months; Td at 10 and 16 years. Mission Indradhanush covers the routine schedule's diseases.
psm.vac.nis.why: A woman vaccinated in a pregnancy within the last 3 years needs only one Td booster.

psm.vac.types.note: Live: BCG, OPV, measles, MR/MMR, rotavirus, yellow fever, varicella, typhoid Ty21a. Killed or subunit: IPV, hepatitis B, DPT components, rabies, typhoid Vi. Live vaccines are avoided in pregnancy and in the immunocompromised. Thiomersal preserves multi-dose DPT, pentavalent and hepatitis B vials.
psm.vac.types.why: Thiomersal is the preservative in DPT; live vaccines like BCG, OPV and MR do not use it.

psm.vac.cold.note: Most sensitive to heat: OPV (then measles). Most sensitive to freezing: hepatitis B, DPT, Td, pentavalent (check with the shake test). Ice-lined refrigerator +2 to +8 °C; deep freezer −15 to −25 °C. Vaccine vial monitor: discard when the square matches or is darker than the circle.
psm.vac.cold.why: A dial thermometer uses a bimetallic strip that bends as temperature changes.

psm.cd.tb.note: Infection (not disease) prevalence is measured with the Mantoux (tuberculin) test. Disease: sputum CBNAAT. Annual risk of TB infection is the best index of TB problem in a community. Treatment under NTEP; notify on Nikshay.
psm.cd.tb.why: The tuberculin (Mantoux) test shows infection, so it is used for infection prevalence surveys.

psm.cd.rabies.note: Category I (touching, licks on intact skin): no treatment. II (nibbling, minor scratches without bleeding): wound wash and vaccine. III (bleeding bites, licks on broken skin or mucosa, any bat contact): wound wash, vaccine and rabies immunoglobulin. Wash with soap and running water for 15 minutes. IM schedule: days 0, 3, 7, 14, 28 (Essen); ID: 0, 3, 7, 28.
psm.cd.rabies.why: Rabies passes through saliva on mucosa or broken skin; eating meat of an infected animal is not a route.

psm.cd.malaria.note: Incubation: falciparum about 12 days, vivax 14, malariae 28. Indices: annual parasite incidence (API) per 1,000, slide positivity rate. India: vivax with chloroquine plus 14-day primaquine; falciparum with ACT (artesunate + sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine; artemether-lumefantrine in the north-east).
psm.cd.malaria.why: Falciparum has the shortest incubation period, about 12 days.

psm.cd.measles.note: Infectious from 4 days before to 4 days after the rash appears; isolate for that time. Secondary attack rate about 80%. Vaccine within 72 hours of exposure can protect; immunoglobulin within 6 days. Give vitamin A to every case.

psm.cd.dengue.note: Aedes aegypti, a day biter that breeds in clean stored water; flight range about 100 m. Larval indices: house index, container index, Breteau index (best). A second infection with a different serotype raises the risk of severe dengue.

psm.cd.hiv.note: Needle-stick risk: hepatitis B about 30%, hepatitis C about 3%, HIV about 0.3%. Post-exposure prophylaxis within 72 hours (best within 2 hours), for 28 days. Mother to child: ART for the mother, nevirapine for the baby.

psm.nhp.ntep.note: National TB Elimination Programme. Nikshay is the online case notification and tracking portal; Nikshay Poshan Yojana pays patients for nutrition. Diagnosis by CBNAAT/TrueNat; daily fixed-dose treatment by weight bands. Goal: end TB in India.
psm.nhp.ntep.why: Nikshay is the web portal for TB notification and patient tracking.

psm.nhp.nacp.note: National AIDS Control Programme: ICTC for testing and counselling, ART centres, PPTCT (prevention of parent-to-child transmission), targeted interventions for high-risk groups, blood safety. Test and treat: ART for everyone diagnosed.

psm.nhp.nvbdcp.note: Covers malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis, kala-azar and filariasis. Long-lasting insecticidal nets use synthetic pyrethroids such as deltamethrin. Filariasis elimination: mass drug administration (DEC with albendazole, plus ivermectin in some areas).
psm.nhp.nvbdcp.why: Insecticide-treated bed nets use pyrethroids such as deltamethrin and cyfluthrin.

psm.nhp.rmnch.note: RMNCH+A covers reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health. JSY (cash for institutional delivery), JSSK (free delivery and newborn care), RBSK (child screening for 4 Ds), RKSK (adolescents), PMSMA (antenatal check on the 9th of every month).

psm.nhp.nhm.note: ASHA: one per 1,000 population (rural), a woman from the village. Home-based newborn care: ASHA visits on days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 after a hospital birth; a home birth adds a visit on day 1. Anganwadi worker under ICDS; ANM at the subcentre.
psm.nhp.nhm.why: Home-based newborn care visits continue up to day 42.

psm.plan.levels.note: Subcentre: 5,000 population in plains (3,000 hilly or tribal). PHC: 30,000 (20,000). CHC: 120,000 (80,000), 30 beds, 4 specialists, the first referral unit. Health and Wellness Centres (Ayushman Arogya Mandir) upgrade subcentres and PHCs.

psm.plan.comm.note: Bhore Committee (1946): the foundation of primary health care in India, the PHC idea. Mudaliar (1962): strengthen PHCs. Kartar Singh (1973): multipurpose workers. Shrivastava (1975): community health volunteers.
psm.plan.comm.why: The Bhore Committee (1946) laid out India's health planning and the primary health centre.

psm.plan.ind.note: HDI: life expectancy, education and income. DALY = years of life lost + years lived with disability. IMR is the best indicator of a community's health and development. Physical Quality of Life Index: IMR, life expectancy at age 1, literacy.

psm.plan.uhc.note: Universal health coverage: everyone gets the services they need without financial hardship. WHO's old target: at least 5% of GNP spent on health. In India, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY covers hospital care up to ₹5 lakh per family per year.
psm.plan.uhc.why: WHO suggested that at least 5% of GNP be spent on health.

psm.scr.crit.note: Wilson and Jungner: an important health problem, a recognisable early stage, an acceptable test, an effective treatment, and a cost that is worth it. Screening is secondary prevention.

psm.scr.bias.note: Lead time bias: screening finds disease earlier, so survival looks longer even if death comes at the same time. Length bias: screening picks up slow-growing disease more often. Selection bias: healthier people volunteer for screening.

psm.nut.vit.note: Vitamin A deficiency: night blindness (earliest), conjunctival xerosis, Bitot spots, keratomalacia. Programme dose: 100,000 IU at 9 months, then 200,000 IU every 6 months to 5 years. Iodine: salt iodised to 30 ppm at production, 15 ppm at the consumer.
psm.nut.vit.why: Dryness of the eyes (xerophthalmia) is caused by vitamin A deficiency.

psm.nut.pem.note: Wasting = low weight-for-height (acute). Stunting = low height-for-age (chronic). Underweight = low weight-for-age (both). SAM: weight-for-height under −3 SD, MUAC under 11.5 cm, or bilateral oedema.
psm.nut.pem.why: Low weight for height is wasting, a sign of acute malnutrition.

psm.nut.prog.note: ICDS (Anganwadi): supplementary food, growth monitoring, preschool education, immunisation. Mid-Day Meal (PM POSHAN): school children. Anaemia Mukt Bharat: iron-folic acid by age group (6x6x6 strategy). POSHAN Abhiyaan targets stunting, anaemia and low birth weight.

psm.mch.anc.note: At least 4 antenatal visits; PMSMA check on the 9th of each month. Iron-folic acid daily from the second trimester for 180 days; calcium; deworming after the first trimester. Average weight gain in pregnancy about 10-12 kg.

psm.mch.ind.note: MMR per 100,000 live births; maternal death up to 42 days after the end of pregnancy. Commonest direct cause: haemorrhage; commonest indirect cause in India: anaemia. IMR per 1,000 live births; perinatal mortality from 28 weeks of pregnancy to 7 days after birth.
psm.mch.ind.why: Anaemia is the commonest indirect cause of maternal death in India.

psm.mch.growth.note: WHO growth charts (2006). Weight-for-height shows wasting; height-for-age shows stunting; weight-for-age shows underweight. The growth chart (road to health) is kept by the mother; a flat or falling line is the earliest warning.

psm.dis.title: Disaster management
psm.dis.note: The disaster cycle: response, rehabilitation, mitigation, preparedness. Triage colours: red (immediate), yellow (urgent), green (walking wounded), black (dead or expectant). After floods, watch for diarrhoea, leptospirosis and vector-borne diseases.

psm.bmw.title: Biomedical waste management
psm.bmw.note: Colour codes (2016 rules): yellow, infectious and anatomical waste, soiled dressings (incinerated); red, contaminated recyclables like tubing, catheters, gloves (autoclaved); white translucent puncture-proof, sharps; blue, glassware and metallic implants. Untreated waste must not be stored beyond 48 hours.

psm.env.title: Environmental health: water, air, sanitation
psm.env.note: Water: chlorine demand, residual free chlorine 0.5 mg/L after 1 hour contact; Horrock's apparatus measures chlorine demand. Coliforms are the indicator of faecal contamination. Fluoride over 1.5 mg/L causes fluorosis. Noise: over 85 dB damages hearing.

psm.occ.title: Occupational health
psm.occ.note: Pneumoconioses: silicosis (the commonest in India; mining, sandblasting), asbestosis (mesothelioma), byssinosis (cotton, Monday fever), bagassosis (sugarcane). Lead poisoning: basophilic stippling, Burton line, wrist drop. ESI Act covers workers' medical and cash benefits. Needle-stick HIV risk is the lowest of the blood-borne viruses.
psm.occ.why: HIV transmission after a needle-stick is about 0.3%, far lower than hepatitis B or C.

psm.he.title: Health education and communication
psm.he.note: Approaches: regulatory, service, health education, primary health care. Communication: one-way lecture vs two-way discussion. Group methods: panel discussion, symposium, workshop, role play. KAP = knowledge, attitude, practice; behaviour change is the aim.

psm.intl.title: SDGs and international health
psm.intl.note: 17 Sustainable Development Goals; goal 3 is good health and well-being, with targets for 2030 (MMR under 70 per 100,000, newborn deaths under 12 per 1,000, under-5 deaths under 25 per 1,000). WHO headquarters is in Geneva; the South-East Asia office is in New Delhi.
